blocks.markdown: # TPS6287Bxx 2.7V to 6V Input, 10A,15A, 20A, 25A, and 30A Fast Transient, Synchronous Step-Down Converter With I<sup>2</sup>C Interface and Remote Sense

blocks.html: 1 Features
blocks.markdown: ## 1 Features

blocks.html:
• • Input voltage range: 2.7V to 6V
  • • Family of pin-to-pin compatible devices: 10A, 15A, 20A, 25A, and 30A
  • • Three selectable output voltage ranges from 0.4V to 1.675V
    • – 0.4V to 0.71875V with 1.25mV steps
    • – 0.4V to 1.0375V with 2.5mV steps
    • – 0.4V to 1.675V with 5mV steps
  • • Output voltage accuracy: ±0.8%
  • • Internal power MOSFETs: 2.6mΩ and 1.5mΩ
  • • Adjustable soft start
  • • External compensation
  • • Selectable start-up output voltage through the VSET1 and VSET2 pins
    • – 0.4V to 0.775V with 25mV of steps
    • – 0.8V to 1.55V with 50mV of steps
  • • Selectable switching frequency of 1.5MHz, 2.25MHz, 2.5MHz, or 3MHz through FSEL pin only for TPS6287BxxJE2 (see Table 4-2)
  • • Forced PWM or power-save mode operation
  • • Start-up output voltage selection by external resistor or I2C
  • • I2C-compatible interface with up to 3.4MHz
  • • Optional stacked operation for increased output current capability
  • • Differential remote sense
  • • Thermal pre-warning and thermal shutdown
  • • Output discharge
  • • Optional spread spectrum clocking
  • • Power-good output with window comparator

blocks.html: 3 Description
blocks.markdown: ## 3 Description

blocks.html: The TPS6287B10, TPS6287B15, TPS6287B20, TPS6287B25, and TPS6287B30 are a family of pin-to-pin, 10A, 15A, 20A, 25A, and 30A synchronous step-down DC/DC converters with I2C interface and differential remote sense. All devices offer high efficiency and ease of use. Low-resistance power switches allow up to 30A output current at high ambient temperature. The devices can operate in stacked mode to deliver higher output currents or to spread the power dissipation across multiple devices.
blocks.markdown: The TPS6287B10, TPS6287B15, TPS6287B20, TPS6287B25, and TPS6287B30 are a family of pin-to-pin, 10A, 15A, 20A, 25A, and 30A synchronous step-down DC/DC converters with I<sup>2</sup>C interface and differential remote sense. All devices offer high efficiency and ease of use. Low-resistance power switches allow up to 30A output current at high ambient temperature. The devices can operate in stacked mode to deliver higher output currents or to spread the power dissipation across multiple devices.

blocks.html: The TPS6287Bxx family implements a fixed-frequency DCS-Control scheme that supports a fast transient response. The devices can operate in power-save mode for maximum efficiency or forced-PWM mode for best transient performance and lowest output voltage ripple.
blocks.markdown: The TPS6287Bxx family implements a fixed-frequency DCS-Control scheme that supports a fast transient response. The devices can operate in power-save mode for maximum efficiency or forced-PWM mode for best transient performance and lowest output voltage ripple.

blocks.html: An optional remote sensing feature maximizes voltage regulation at the point-of-load, and the device achieves ±0.8% DC voltage accuracy for the full output voltage range.
blocks.markdown: An optional remote sensing feature maximizes voltage regulation at the point-of-load, and the device achieves ±0.8% DC voltage accuracy for the full output voltage range.

blocks.html: The I2C compatible interface offers several control, monitoring and warning features, such as voltage monitoring and temperature related warnings. The output voltage can be quickly adjusted to adapt the load's power consumption to the performance needs. The default start-up voltage is resistor selectable through the VSET1 and VSET2 pins.

blocks.html: Simplified Schematic diagram of the TPS6287Bxx converter. It shows the input section with VIN (2.7V to 6V), VIN pin, and a soft-start network with R_EN and C_IN. The converter core includes MODE/SYNC, EN, SDA, SCL, VSET1, VSET2, COMP, PG, SYNC_OUT, AGND, and GND pins. The output section features a power switch (SW), an inductor (L), an output capacitor (COUT), and a load. A remote sense network with R_Z, C_C, and C_C2 is connected to the VOSNS and GOSNS pins. A power-good output (PG) is shown with a resistor R_PG and a capacitor C_C2.

During start-up, this pin is used to identify if a device must operate as a secondary converter in stacked operation. Connect a 47kΩ resistor from this pin to GND to define a secondary converter in stacked operation. See Section 8.3.18 for a detailed description.
18MODE/SYNCIThe device runs in Power-Save mode when this pin is pulled low. If the pin is pulled high, the device runs in Forced-PWM mode. Do not leave this pin unconnected. The mode pin can also be used to synchronize the device to an external clock.

20SCLI/OI2C serial clock pin. Do not leave this pin floating. Connect a pullup resistor to a logic high level. Connect to GND for secondary devices in stacked operation.
21PGI/OOpen drain power-good output. Low impedance when not "power good", high impedance when "power good". This pin can be left open or be tied to GND when not used in single device operation.
In stacked operation interconnect the PG pins of all stacked devices. Only the PG pin of the primary converter in stacked operation is an open drain output. For devices that are defined as secondary converters in stacked mode the pin is an input pin. See Section 8.3.18 for a detailed description.
22AGNDGNDAnalog Ground. Connect to GND.
23COMP—Device compensation input. A resistor and capacitor from this pin to AGND define the compensation of the control loop.
In stacked operation connect the COMP pins of all stacked devices together and connect a resistor and capacitor between the common COMP node and AGND.
24GOSNS—Output ground sense (differential output voltage sensing)

blocks.markdown: ## 8 Detailed Description

blocks.html: 8.1 Overview
blocks.markdown: ### 8.1 Overview

blocks.html: The TPS6287Bxx devices are synchronous step-down (buck) DC/DC converters. These devices use an enhanced DCS-Control scheme that combines fast transient response with fixed frequency operation, which, together with the low output voltage ripple, high DC accuracy and differential remote sensing makes them designed for supplying the cores of modern high-performance processors.
blocks.markdown: The TPS6287Bxx devices are synchronous step-down (buck) DC/DC converters. These devices use an enhanced DCS-Control scheme that combines fast transient response with fixed frequency operation, which, together with the low output voltage ripple, high DC accuracy and differential remote sensing makes them designed for supplying the cores of modern high-performance processors.

blocks.html: The three devices in this family are identical except for the current rating:
blocks.markdown: The three devices in this family are identical except for the current rating:

blocks.html:
• • The TPS6287B10 is a 10A rated device.
  • • The TPS6287B15 is a 15A rated device.
  • • The TPS6287B20 is a 20A rated device.
  • • The TPS6287B25 is a 25A rated device.
  • • The TPS6287B30 is a 30A rated device.
blocks.markdown:
- The TPS6287B10 is a 10A rated device.
- The TPS6287B15 is a 15A rated device.
- The TPS6287B20 is a 20A rated device.
- The TPS6287B25 is a 25A rated device.
- The TPS6287B30 is a 30A rated device.

blocks.html: To further increase the output current capability, combine multiple devices in a stack. For example, a stack of two TPS6287B25 devices has a current capability of 50A.
blocks.markdown: To further increase the output current capability, combine multiple devices in a *stack*. For example, a stack of two TPS6287B25 devices has a current capability of 50A.

blocks.html: The TPS6287Bxx devices have a built-in I2C-compatible interface to control and monitor the operation. If the I2C-compatible interface is not used, connect the SCL and SDA pins to GND.
blocks.markdown: The TPS6287Bxx devices have a built-in I<sup>2</sup>C-compatible interface to control and monitor the operation. If the I<sup>2</sup>C-compatible interface is not used, connect the SCL and SDA pins to GND.

The functional block diagram illustrates the internal architecture of the TPS6287Bxx DC/DC converter. The diagram shows the following components and their connections:

  • Input Section: Four VIN pins are connected to the input voltage. A Bias Regulator is connected to these pins and provides power to the Device Control block.
  • Control Section: The EN (Enable) pin is connected to the Device Control block. The PG (Power Good) pin is connected to the Device Control block and includes a 3 M\Omega pull-up resistor and a protection diode. The MODE/SYNC pin is connected to the Device Control block and includes a 3 M\Omega pull-up resistor.
  • Output Section: The SW (Switch) pins are connected to the output of the Gate Drive and Control block. The GND pins are connected to ground. The VOSNS (Output Sensing) and GOSNS (Ground Sensing) pins are connected to the output of the Ramp and Slope Compensation block. The COMP (Compensation) pin is connected to the output of the Ramp and Slope Compensation block. The AGND (Analog Ground) and SYNC_OUT (Synchronization Output) pins are connected to ground.
  • Internal Components:
    • Gate Drive and Control: This block controls the power switches and includes current sense amplifiers (IHS and ILS).
    • Device Control: This block manages the overall operation of the converter.
    • Oscillator: Provides a clock signal to the Gate Drive and Control block.
    • Thermal Shutdown: Monitors the temperature and provides a shutdown signal to the Device Control block.
    • Ramp and Slope Compensation: Provides compensation for the control loop.
    • Transconductance Amplifier (gm): Amplifies the error signal from the feedback loop.
    • Reference Voltage (VREF): Provides a stable reference voltage for the feedback loop.

blocks.html: Figure 8-1 shows a simplified block diagram of the fixed-frequency DCS-Control topology used in the TPS6287Bxx devices. This topology comprises an inner emulated current loop and an outer voltage-regulating loop.
blocks.markdown: Figure 8-1 shows a simplified block diagram of the fixed-frequency DCS-Control topology used in the TPS6287Bxx devices. This topology comprises an inner emulated current loop and an outer voltage-regulating loop.

blocks.html: Figure 8-1: Fixed-Frequency DCS-Control Topology (Simplified). This block diagram illustrates the control architecture. It features a feedback loop where the output voltage (VOUT) is compared with a reference voltage (VREF) using an error amplifier. The error signal is processed by 'Control Logic' which includes a frequency source (fsw) and a switch (SW) to generate an 'ON' signal. This signal drives a 'Gate Driver' for the power switch (MOSFET). The output stage consists of an inductor (L) and a capacitor (COUT) connected to the load (RLoad). A 'Slope Compensation' block is shown, which is part of the control logic and provides a feedback signal (VOSNS) to the error amplifier. The error amplifier also receives a feedback signal (GOSNS) from the output stage. The diagram also shows various ground connections (AGND, GND) and capacitors (C1, C2) for stability and decoupling.

blocks.html: The device can control the inductor current in three different ways to regulate the output:
blocks.markdown: The device can control the inductor current in three different ways to regulate the output:

blocks.html:
• • Pulse-width modulation with continuous inductor current (PWM-CCM)
  • • Pulse-width modulation with discontinuous inductor current (PWM-DCM)
  • • Pulse-frequency modulation with discontinuous inductor current and pulse skipping (PFM-CCM)
blocks.markdown:
- Pulse-width modulation with continuous inductor current (PWM-CCM)
- Pulse-width modulation with discontinuous inductor current (PWM-DCM)
- Pulse-frequency modulation with discontinuous inductor current and pulse skipping (PFM-CCM)

blocks.html: During PWM-CCM operation, the device switches at a constant frequency and the inductor current is continuous (see Figure 8-2). PWM operation achieves the lowest output voltage ripple and the best transient performance.

blocks.html: 8.3.3 Transient Non-Synchronous Mode (optional)
blocks.markdown: #### 8.3.3 Transient Non-Synchronous Mode (optional)

blocks.html: The TPS6287Bxx has a transient non-synchronous mode that helps to minimize the output voltage overshoot during a load release. When the high side FET is turned off, the decay in inductor current is mainly determined by the output voltage as there is little voltage drop over the low side FET. For very low output voltages the current decays slowly so the output voltage overshoot is typically larger than the undershoot during a load step. Non-synchronous mode turns off the low side FET for 6 switching cycles so the inductor current decays through the body diode. This adds extra voltage across the inductor so the current decays quicker and the output voltage overshoot is lower.

blocks.html: When power is first applied to the VIN pin, the device pulls the EN pin low until the device has loaded the default register settings from nonvolatile memory and read the state of the VSET1, VSET2 and SYNC_OUT pins. The device also pulls EN low if a fault such as thermal shutdown or overvoltage lockout occurs. In a stacked configuration all devices share a common enable signal, which means that the DC/DC converters in the stack cannot start to switch until all devices in the stack have completed the initialization. Similarly, a fault in one or more devices in the stack disables all converters in the stack (see Section 8.3.18).

blocks.html: 8.3.5 Start-Up
blocks.markdown: #### 8.3.5 Start-Up

blocks.html: When the voltage on the VIN pin exceeds the positive-going UVLO threshold, the device initializes as follows:
blocks.markdown: When the voltage on the VIN pin exceeds the positive-going UVLO threshold, the device initializes as follows:

blocks.html:
• • The device pulls the EN pin low.
  • • The device enables the internal reference voltage.
  • • The device reads the state of the VSET1, VSET2, VSET3, VSET4, FSET and SYNC_OUT pins.
  • • The device loads the default values into the device registers.
blocks.markdown:
- The device pulls the EN pin low.
- The device enables the internal reference voltage.
- The device reads the state of the VSET1, VSET2, VSET3, VSET4, FSET and SYNC\_OUT pins.
- The device loads the default values into the device registers.

blocks.html: When initialization is complete, the device enables I2C communication and releases the EN pin. The external circuitry controlling the EN pin now determines the behavior of the device:
blocks.markdown: When initialization is complete, the device enables I<sup>2</sup>C communication and releases the EN pin. The external circuitry controlling the EN pin now determines the behavior of the device:

blocks.html:
• • If the EN pin is low, the device is disabled: write to and read from the device registers, but the DC/DC converter does not operate.
  • • If the EN pin is high, the device is enabled: write to and read from the device registers and, after a short delay from EN pin going high, the DC/DC converter starts to ramp up the output.
blocks.markdown:
- If the EN pin is low, the device is disabled: write to and read from the device registers, but the DC/DC converter does not operate.
- If the EN pin is high, the device is enabled: write to and read from the device registers and, after a short delay from EN pin going high, the DC/DC converter starts to ramp up the output.

blocks.html: 8.3.7.5 Droop Compensation
blocks.markdown: ##### 8.3.7.5 Droop Compensation

blocks.html: Droop compensation scales the nominal output voltage based on the output current. This action is done such that the output voltage is set to a higher value with no output current and to a lower value than the nominal value with the maximum output current. Droop compensation therefore provides a higher margin during a load transient and helps to keep the output voltage within a certain tolerance band in case of a heavy load step or at load release or allows to use a lower output capacitance. The voltage scaling is absolute instead of relative. The voltage scaling vs output current depends on the output current version of TPS6287Bxx based on the rated output current of 10A, 15A, 20A, 25A and 30A, respectively. The behavior is shown in the graph in Figure 8-11. See the Device Options table for the specific version if droop compensation is disabled or enabled by default. Droop compensation can be enabled by bit CONTROL3:DROOPEN. Enabling droop compensation must be done while the device is disabled otherwise a transient output voltage deviation can occur.

This action is done such that the output voltage is set to a higher value with no output current and to a lower value than the nominal value with the maximum output current. The voltage scaling is absolute instead of relative. The behavior is shown in the graph in [Figure 8-11](#). See the [Device Options](#) table for the specific version if droop compensation is disabled or enabled by default. Droop compensation can be enabled by bit CONTROL3:DROOPEN. Enabling droop compensation must be done while the device is disabled otherwise a transient output voltage deviation can occur.

blocks.html: 8.3.8 Compensation (COMP)
blocks.markdown: #### 8.3.8 Compensation (COMP)

blocks.html: The COMP pin is the connection point for an external compensation network. A series-connected resistor and capacitor to AGND is sufficient for typical applications and provides enough scope to optimize the loop response for a wide range of operating conditions.
blocks.markdown: The COMP pin is the connection point for an external compensation network. A series-connected resistor and capacitor to AGND is sufficient for typical applications and provides enough scope to optimize the loop response for a wide range of operating conditions.

blocks.html: When using multiple devices in a stacked configuration, all devices share a common compensation network, and the COMP pin makes sure of equal current sharing between the devices (see Section 8.3.18).
blocks.markdown: When using multiple devices in a stacked configuration, all devices share a common compensation network, and the COMP pin makes sure of equal current sharing between the devices (see [Section 8.3.18](#)).

blocks.html: 8.3.9 Mode Selection / Clock Synchronization (MODE/SYNC)
blocks.markdown: #### 8.3.9 Mode Selection / Clock Synchronization (MODE/SYNC)

blocks.html: A high level on the MODE/SYNC pin selects forced-PWM operation. A low level on the MODE/SYNC pin selects power-save operation, in which the device automatically transitions between PWM and PFM, according to the load conditions.
blocks.markdown: A high level on the MODE/SYNC pin selects forced-PWM operation. A low level on the MODE/SYNC pin selects power-save operation, in which the device automatically transitions between PWM and PFM, according to the load conditions.

blocks.html: If you apply a valid clock signal to the MODE/SYNC pin, the device synchronizes the switching cycles to the external clock and automatically selects forced-PWM operation.
blocks.markdown: If you apply a valid clock signal to the MODE/SYNC pin, the device synchronizes the switching cycles to the external clock and automatically selects forced-PWM operation.

blocks.html: The MODE/SYNC pin is logically ORed with the FPWMEN bit in the CONTROL1 register (see Table 8-1).
blocks.markdown: The MODE/SYNC pin is logically ORed with the FPWMEN bit in the CONTROL1 register (see [Table 8-1](#)).

blocks.html: When multiple devices are used together in a stacked configuration the MODE/SYNC pin of the secondary devices is the input for the clock signal (see Section 8.3.18).
blocks.markdown: When multiple devices are used together in a stacked configuration the MODE/SYNC pin of the secondary devices is the input for the clock signal (see [Section 8.3.18](#)).

blocks.markdown: #### 8.3.10 Spread Spectrum Clocking (SSC)

blocks.html: The device has a spread spectrum clocking function that can reduce electromagnetic interference (EMI). When the SSC function is active, the device modulates the switching frequency \pm 10\% about the nominal value. The frequency modulation has a triangular characteristic (see Figure 8-12).

When the SSC function is active, the device modulates the switching frequency  $\pm 10\%$  about the nominal value. The frequency modulation has a triangular characteristic (see [Figure 8-12](#)).

blocks.html: 8.3.11 Output Discharge
blocks.markdown: #### **8.3.11 Output Discharge**

blocks.html: The device has an output discharge function which makes sure of a defined ramp down of the output voltage when the device is disabled and keeps the output voltage close to 0V while the device is off. The output discharge function is enabled when DISCHEN = 1 in the CONTROL1 register. The output discharge function is enabled by default.
blocks.markdown: The device has an output discharge function which makes sure of a defined ramp down of the output voltage when the device is disabled and keeps the output voltage close to 0V while the device is off. The output discharge function is enabled when DISCHEN = 1 in the CONTROL1 register. The output discharge function is enabled by default.

blocks.html: If enabled, the device discharges the output under the following conditions:
blocks.markdown: If enabled, the device discharges the output under the following conditions:

blocks.html:
• • A low level is applied to the EN pin
  • • SWEN = 0 in the CONTROL1 register
  • • A thermal shutdown event occurs
  • • An UVLO event occurs
  • • An OVLO event occurs
blocks.markdown:
- A low level is applied to the EN pin
- SWEN = 0 in the CONTROL1 register
- A thermal shutdown event occurs
- An UVLO event occurs
- An OVLO event occurs

blocks.html: The output discharge function is not available until you have enabled the device at least once after power up. During power-down, the device continues to discharge the output for as long as the supply voltage is greater than approximately 1.8V.
blocks.markdown: The output discharge function is not available until you have enabled the device at least once after power up. During power-down, the device continues to discharge the output for as long as the supply voltage is greater than approximately 1.8V.

blocks.html: 8.3.12 Undervoltage Lockout (UVLO)
blocks.markdown: #### **8.3.12 Undervoltage Lockout (UVLO)**

blocks.html: The TPS6287Bxx has an undervoltage lockout function that disables the device if the supply voltage is too low for correct operation. The negative-going threshold of the UVLO function is 2.5V (typical). If the supply voltage decreases below this value, the device stops switching and, if DISCHEN = 1 in the CONTROL1 register, turns on the output discharge.
blocks.markdown: The TPS6287Bxx has an undervoltage lockout function that disables the device if the supply voltage is too low for correct operation. The negative-going threshold of the UVLO function is 2.5V (typical). If the supply voltage decreases below this value, the device stops switching and, if DISCHEN = 1 in the CONTROL1 register, turns on the output discharge.

blocks.html: 8.3.13 Overvoltage Lockout (OVLO)
blocks.markdown: #### **8.3.13 Overvoltage Lockout (OVLO)**

blocks.html: The TPS6287Bxx has an overvoltage lockout function that disables the DC/DC converter if the supply voltage is too high for correct operation. The positive-going threshold of the OVLO function is 6.3V (typical). If the supply voltage increases above this value, the device stops switching and, if DISCHEN = 1 in the CONTROL1 register, turns on the output discharge.
blocks.markdown: The TPS6287Bxx has an overvoltage lockout function that disables the DC/DC converter if the supply voltage is too high for correct operation. The positive-going threshold of the OVLO function is 6.3V (typical). If the supply voltage increases above this value, the device stops switching and, if DISCHEN = 1 in the CONTROL1 register, turns on the output discharge.

blocks.html: The device automatically starts switching again – the device begins a new soft-start sequence – when the supply voltage falls below 6.2V (typical).

blocks.html: 8.3.14.2 Hiccup Mode
blocks.markdown: ##### 8.3.14.2 Hiccup Mode

blocks.html: To enable hiccup operation, make sure that HICCUPEN = 1 in the CONTROL1 register. The HICCUP function is disabled by default.
blocks.markdown: To enable hiccup operation, make sure that HICCUPEN = 1 in the CONTROL1 register. The HICCUP function is disabled by default.

blocks.html: If hiccup operation is enabled and the high-side switch current exceeds the current limit threshold on 32 consecutive switching cycles, the device:
blocks.markdown: If hiccup operation is enabled and the high-side switch current exceeds the current limit threshold on 32 consecutive switching cycles, the device:

blocks.html:
• • Stops switching for 128µs, after which the device automatically starts switching again (starts a new soft-start sequence).
  • • Sets the HICCUP bit in the STATUS register.
  • • Pulls the PG pin low. The PG pin stays low until the overload condition goes away and the device can start up correctly and regulate the output voltage. Note that power-good function has a deglitch circuit, which delays the rising edge of the power-good signal by 40µs (typical).
blocks.markdown:
- Stops switching for 128µs, after which the device automatically starts switching again (starts a new soft-start sequence).
- Sets the HICCUP bit in the STATUS register.
- Pulls the PG pin low. The PG pin stays low until the overload condition goes away and the device can start up correctly and regulate the output voltage. Note that power-good function has a deglitch circuit, which delays the rising edge of the power-good signal by 40µs (typical).

blocks.html: Hiccup operation continues – in a repeating sequence of 32 cycles in current limit, followed by a pause of 128µs, followed by a soft-start attempt – for as long as the output overload condition exists.

blocks.html: The device clears the HICCUP bit if you read the STATUS register when the overload condition has been removed.

blocks.html: To enable current-limit mode, make sure that HICCUPEN = 0 in the CONTROL1 register.

blocks.html: When current limit operation is enabled, the device limits the high-side switch current cycle-by-cycle for as long as the overload condition exists. If the device limits the high-side switch current for four or more consecutive switching cycle, the device sets ILIM = 1 in the STATUS register.

If the device limits the high-side switch current for four or more consecutive switching cycle, the device sets ILIM = 1 in the STATUS register.

blocks.html: The device clears the ILIM bit if the user reads the STATUS register when the overload condition no longer exists.

blocks.html: Figure 8-14 shows a functional block diagram of the power-good function in a stand-alone or primary device. A window comparator monitors the output voltage, and the output of the comparator goes high if the output voltage is either less than 95% (typical) or greater than 105% (typical) of the nominal output voltage. The output of the window comparator is deglitched – the typical deglitch time is 40μs – and then used to drive the open-drain PG pin.

blocks.html: Figure 8-14. Power-Good Functional Block Diagram (Standalone / Primary Device). The diagram shows the internal logic for power-good detection. It includes a Hiccup Control block receiving CONTROL1:HICCUPEN and outputting to converter control logic and a STATUS Register. The STATUS Register outputs PBOV, PBUV, ILIM, and HICCUP. A Current Comparator receives Isw and feeds into the Hiccup Control and a 4 Consecutive Pulses Detection block, which also feeds into the STATUS Register. A Window Comparator receives Vout and a 95% to 105% Vout window, outputting to a 40-µs Deglitch block, which then feeds into a Blanking block. The Blanking block also receives DVS Active and CONTROL3:PGBLNKDVS signals. The Blanking block output and the STATUS Register's HICCUP output are combined with Thermal Shutdown conditions (VIn > VIT(OVLO), VIn < VIT(UVLO), VEn < VIT(EN)) in an OR gate to control the PG pin via a PMOS transistor.

blocks.html: 8.3.15.2 Secondary Device Behavior
blocks.markdown: ##### 8.3.15.2 Secondary Device Behavior

blocks.html: Figure 8-15 shows a functional block diagram of the power-good function in a secondary device. During initialization, the device presets FF2, which pulls down the PG pin and forces the devices in a stack to operate in DCM. When the device completes the internal start-up sequence, the device resets FF2, which turns off Q1. In a stacked configuration all devices share the same PG signal, and therefore the PG pin stays low until all devices in the stack have completed the start-up. When that happens, FF1 is set and the converters operate in CCM. FF1 and FF2 are preset such that DCM is allowed each time the converter is disabled, either by the EN pin, EN bit, thermal shutdown or UVLO.

In a stacked configuration all devices share the same PG signal, and therefore the PG pin stays low until *all* devices in the stack have completed the start-up. When that happens, FF1 is set and the converters operate in CCM. FF1 and FF2 are preset such that DCM is allowed each time the converter is disabled, either by the EN pin, EN bit, thermal shutdown or UVLO.

blocks.html: 8.3.16 Remote Sense
blocks.markdown: #### 8.3.16 Remote Sense

blocks.html: The device has two pins, VOSNS and GOSNS, to remotely sense the output voltage. Remote sensing lets the converter sense the output voltage directly at the point-of-load and increases the accuracy of the output voltage regulation.
blocks.markdown: The device has two pins, VOSNS and GOSNS, to remotely sense the output voltage. Remote sensing lets the converter sense the output voltage directly at the point-of-load and increases the accuracy of the output voltage regulation.

blocks.html: In a stacked configuration, you must connect the VOSNS and GOSNS of the primary device directly at the point-of-load. For the secondary devices, you can connect the VOSNS and GOSNS pins to the local output capacitor or both pins to AGND (see Section 8.3.18).
blocks.markdown: In a stacked configuration, you must connect the VOSNS and GOSNS of the primary device directly at the point-of-load. For the secondary devices, you can connect the VOSNS and GOSNS pins to the local output capacitor or both pins to AGND (see [Section 8.3.18](#)).

blocks.html: 8.3.17 Thermal Warning and Shutdown
blocks.markdown: #### 8.3.17 Thermal Warning and Shutdown

blocks.html: The device has a two-level overtemperature detection function.
blocks.markdown: The device has a two-level overtemperature detection function.

blocks.html: If the junction temperature rises above the thermal warning threshold of 150 °C (typical), the device sets the TWARN bit in the STATUS register. The device clears the TWARN bit if you read the STATUS register when the junction temperature is below the TWARN threshold of 130°C (typical).
blocks.markdown: If the junction temperature rises above the thermal warning threshold of 150 °C (typical), the device sets the TWARN bit in the STATUS register. The device clears the TWARN bit if you read the STATUS register when the junction temperature is below the TWARN threshold of 130°C (typical).

blocks.html: If the junction temperature rises above the thermal shutdown threshold of 170°C (typical), the device:
blocks.markdown: If the junction temperature rises above the thermal shutdown threshold of 170°C (typical), the device:

blocks.html:
• • Stops switching
  • • Pulls down the EN pin (if SINGLE = 0 in the CONTROL3 register)
  • • Enables the output discharge (if DISCHEN = 1 in the CONTROL1 register)
  • • Sets the TSHUT bit in the STATUS register
  • • Pulls the PG pin low
blocks.markdown:
- Stops switching
- Pulls down the EN pin (if SINGLE = 0 in the CONTROL3 register)
- Enables the output discharge (if DISCHEN = 1 in the CONTROL1 register)
- Sets the TSHUT bit in the STATUS register
- Pulls the PG pin low

blocks.html: If the junction temperature falls below the thermal shutdown threshold of 150°C (typical), the device:
blocks.markdown: If the junction temperature falls below the thermal shutdown threshold of 150°C (typical), the device:

blocks.html:
• • Starts switching again, starting with a new soft-start sequence
  • • Sets the EN pin to high impedance
  • • Sets the PG pin to high-impedance
blocks.markdown:
- Starts switching again, starting with a new soft-start sequence
- Sets the EN pin to high impedance
- Sets the PG pin to high-impedance

blocks.html: The device clears the TSHUT bit if you read the STATUS register when the junction temperature is below the TSHUT threshold of 150°C (typical).
blocks.markdown: The device clears the TSHUT bit if you read the STATUS register when the junction temperature is below the TSHUT threshold of 150°C (typical).

blocks.html: In a stacked configuration, in which all devices share a common enable signal, a thermal shutdown condition in one device disables the entire stack. When the hot device cools down, the whole stack automatically starts switching again.
blocks.markdown: In a stacked configuration, in which all devices share a common enable signal, a thermal shutdown condition in one device disables the entire stack. When the hot device cools down, the whole stack automatically starts switching again.

blocks.html: 8.3.18 Stacked Operation
blocks.markdown: #### 8.3.18 Stacked Operation

blocks.html: Connect multiple TPS6287Bxx devices in parallel in what is known as a "stack"; for example, to increase output current capability or reduce device junction temperature. A stack comprises one primary device and one or more secondary devices. During initialization, each device monitors the SYNCOUT pin to determine if the device must operate as a primary device or a secondary device:
blocks.markdown: Connect multiple TPS6287Bxx devices in parallel in what is known as a "stack"; for example, to increase output current capability or reduce device junction temperature. A stack comprises one *primary* device and one or more *secondary* devices. During initialization, each device monitors the SYNCOUT pin to determine if the device must operate as a primary device or a secondary device:

blocks.html:
• • If there is a 47\text{k}\Omega resistor between the SYNCOUT pin and ground, the device operates as a secondary device
  • • If the SYNCOUT pin is high impedance, the device operates as a primary device
blocks.markdown:
- If there is a  $47\text{k}\Omega$  resistor between the SYNCOUT pin and ground, the device operates as a secondary device
- If the SYNCOUT pin is high impedance, the device operates as a primary device

blocks.html: In a stacked configuration, the common enable signal also acts as a SYSTEM_READY signal (see Section 8.3.4). Each device in the stack can pull the EN pin low during device start-up or when a fault occurs. Thus, the stack is only enabled when all devices have completed the start-up sequence and are fault-free. A fault in any one device disables the whole stack for as long as the fault condition exists.

Each device in the stack can pull the EN pin low during device start-up or when a fault occurs. blocks.html: During start-up, the primary device pulls the COMP pin low for as long as the enable signal (SYSTEM_READY) is low. When the enable signal goes high, the primary device actively controls the COMP pin and all devices in the stack follow the COMP voltage. During start-up, each device in the stack pulls the PG pin low while the pin initializes. When initialization is complete, each secondary device in the stack sets the PG pin to a high impedance and the primary device alone controls the state of the PG signal. The PG pin goes high when the stack has completed the start-up ramp and the output voltage is within specification. The secondary devices in the stack detect the rising edge of the power-good signal and switch from DCM operation to CCM operation. After the stack has successfully started up, the primary device controls the power-good signal in the normal way. In a stacked configuration, there are some faults that only affect individual devices, and other faults that affect all devices. For example, if one device enters current limit, only that device is affected. But a thermal shutdown or undervoltage lockout event in one device disables all devices through the shared enable (SYSTEM_READY) signal.

blocks.html: 8.5.1 Serial Interface Description
blocks.markdown: #### 8.5.1 Serial Interface Description

blocks.html: I2C™ is a 2-wire serial interface developed by Philips Semiconductor, now NXP Semiconductors (see I2C-Bus Specification and User's Manual, Revision 6, 4 April 2014). The bus consists of a data line (SDA) and a clock line (SCL) with pull-up structures. When the bus is idle, both SDA and SCL lines are pulled high. All the I2C compatible devices connect to the I2C bus through open drain I/O pins, SDA and SCL. A controller, usually a microcontroller or a digital signal processor, controls the bus. The controller is responsible for generating the SCL signal and device addresses. The controller also generates specific conditions that indicate the START and STOP of data transfer. A target receives or transmits data on the bus under control of the controller.
blocks.markdown: I<sup>2</sup>C™ is a 2-wire serial interface developed by Philips Semiconductor, now NXP Semiconductors (see I<sup>2</sup>C-Bus Specification and User's Manual, Revision 6, 4 April 2014). The bus consists of a data line (SDA) and a clock line (SCL) with pull-up structures. When the bus is *idle*, both SDA and SCL lines are pulled high. All the I<sup>2</sup>C compatible devices connect to the I<sup>2</sup>C bus through open drain I/O pins, SDA and SCL. A controller, usually a microcontroller or a digital signal processor, controls the bus. The controller is responsible for generating the SCL signal and device addresses. The controller also generates specific conditions that indicate the START and STOP of data transfer. A target receives or transmits data on the bus under control of the controller.

blocks.html: The controller then generates the SCL pulses, and transmits the 7-bit address and the read/write direction bit R/W on the SDA line. During all transmissions, the controller makes sure that data is valid. A valid data condition requires the SDA line to be stable during the entire high period of the clock pulse (see Figure 8-18). Upon detecting this acknowledge, the controller knows that the communication link with a target has been established.

This releases the bus and stops the communication link with the addressed target. All I2C compatible devices must recognize the stop condition. Upon the receipt of a stop condition, all devices know that the bus is released, and the devices wait for a start condition followed by a matching address.

blocks.html: 8.5.3 HS-Mode Protocol
blocks.markdown: #### **8.5.3 HS-Mode Protocol**

blocks.html: The controller generates a start condition followed by a valid serial byte containing HS controller code 00001XXX. This transmission is made in F/S-mode at no more than 400Kbps. No device is allowed to acknowledge the HS controller code, but all devices must recognize the code and switch the internal setting to support 3.4Mbps operation.
blocks.markdown: The controller generates a start condition followed by a valid serial byte containing HS controller code 00001XXX. This transmission is made in F/S-mode at no more than 400Kbps. No device is allowed to acknowledge the HS controller code, but all devices must recognize the code and switch the internal setting to support 3.4Mbps operation.

blocks.html: The controller then generates a repeated start condition (a repeated start condition has the same timing as the start condition). After this repeated start condition, the protocol is the same as F/S-mode, except that transmission speeds up to 3.4Mbps are allowed. A stop condition ends the HS-mode and switches all the internal settings of the target devices to support the F/S-mode. Instead of using a stop condition, repeated start conditions must be used to secure the bus in HS-mode.
blocks.markdown: The controller then generates a *repeated start condition* (a repeated start condition has the same timing as the start condition). After this repeated start condition, the protocol is the same as F/S-mode, except that transmission speeds up to 3.4Mbps are allowed. A stop condition ends the HS-mode and switches all the internal settings of the target devices to support the F/S-mode. Instead of using a stop condition, repeated start conditions must be used to secure the bus in HS-mode.

blocks.html: This requires a start condition, a valid I2C address, a register address byte, and a data byte for a single update. The device performs an update on the falling edge of the acknowledge signal that follows the LSB byte.

blocks.html: 8.5.6 Dynamic Voltage Scaling (DVS)
blocks.markdown: #### **8.5.6 Dynamic Voltage Scaling (DVS)**

blocks.html: To optimize the power consumption of the system, the output voltage of the TPS6287Bxx can be adapted during operation based on the actual power requirement of the load.
blocks.markdown: To optimize the power consumption of the system, the output voltage of the TPS6287Bxx can be adapted during operation based on the actual power requirement of the load.

blocks.html: The device starts up into the default output voltage selected through the external VSET1 and VSET2 pins or the settings in the VSET register. The output voltage can be dynamically adapted through the I2C interface by writing the new target output voltage to the VSET register. The output voltage then increases or decrease to the desired value with the voltage ramp speed defined in the CONTROL1 register.

The output voltage can be dynamically adapted through the I<sup>2</sup>C interface by writing the new target output voltage to the VSET register. The output voltage then increases or decrease to the desired value with the voltage ramp speed defined in the CONTROL1 register.

blocks.html: Switching between different output voltage ranges
blocks.markdown: ##### **Switching between different output voltage ranges**

blocks.html: TPS6287Bxx devices offer three different output voltages ranges as defined in the CONTROL2 register. To change the output voltage range of TPS6287Bxx, first step to the closest output voltage value within the currently used range, then change the VRANGE bit in the CONTROL2 register to the next VRANGE setting. After that set the target output voltage in the VSET register.

To change the output voltage range of TPS6287Bxx, first step to the closest output voltage value within the currently used range, then change the VRANGE bit in the CONTROL2 register to the next VRANGE setting. After that set the target output voltage in the VSET register.

blocks.html: Note that a change in the output voltage range always must be followed by writing to the VSET Register, even though the output voltage does not change. The code in the VSET register must be updated to the correct value in the new range.

blocks.html: 10.2.2.1 Inductor Selection
blocks.markdown: ##### **10.2.2.1 Inductor Selection**

blocks.html: The TPS6287Bxx devices have been optimized for inductors in the range 100nH to 200nH. If the transient response of the converter is limited by the slew rate of the current in the inductor, using a smaller inductor can improve performance. However, the output ripple current increases as the value of the inductor decreases, and higher output current ripple generates higher output voltage ripple, which adds to the transient over or undershoot. The optimum configuration for a given application is a trade-off between a number of parameters. TI recommends a starting value of 105nH for typical applications.

10.2.2.2 Selecting the Input Capacitors
blocks.markdown: ##### 10.2.2.2 Selecting the Input Capacitors

blocks.html: As with all buck converters, the input current of the TPS6287Bxx devices is discontinuous. The input capacitors provide a low-impedance energy source for the device, and the value, type, and location are critical for correct operation. TI recommends low-ESR multilayer ceramic capacitors for best performance. In practice, the total input capacitance typically comprises a combination of different capacitors, in which larger capacitors provide the decoupling at lower frequencies and smaller capacitors provide the decoupling at higher frequencies.

The input capacitors provide a low-impedance energy source for the device, and the value, type, and location are critical for correct operation. In practice, the total input capacitance typically comprises a combination of different capacitors, in which larger capacitors provide the decoupling at lower frequencies and smaller capacitors provide the decoupling at higher frequencies.

blocks.html: The TPS6287Bxx devices feature a butterfly layout with two VIN pin pairs on opposite sides of the package. This allows the input capacitors to be placed symmetrically on the PCB such that the electromagnetic fields generated cancel each other out, thereby reducing EMI.

blocks.html: In this case, choose C_{OUT(min)} = 195 \mu F, as the larger of the two values, for the output capacitance.
blocks.markdown: In this case, choose  $C_{OUT(min)} = 195 \mu F$ , as the larger of the two values, for the output capacitance.

blocks.html: When calculating worst-case component values, use the value calculated above as the minimum output capacitance required. For ceramic capacitors, the nominal capacitance when considering tolerance, DC bias, temperature, and aging effects is typically two times the minimum capacitance. In this case, the nominal capacitance is thus 390 \mu F.
blocks.markdown: When calculating worst-case component values, use the value calculated above as the *minimum* output capacitance required. For ceramic capacitors, the *nominal* capacitance when considering tolerance, DC bias, temperature, and aging effects is typically two times the minimum capacitance. In this case, the nominal capacitance is thus  $390 \mu F$ .

10.2.2.5 Selecting the Compensation Capacitor C_C
blocks.markdown: ##### 10.2.2.5 Selecting the Compensation Capacitor $C_C$

blocks.html: First, use Equation 18 to calculate the bandwidth of the loop:
blocks.markdown: First, use [Equation 18](#) to calculate the bandwidth of the loop:

blocks.html: BW = \frac{\tau \times g_m \times R_Z}{2 \times \pi \times L \times C_{OUT,min} \times k_{COUT}} \quad (18)
blocks.markdown: $$BW = \frac{\tau \times g_m \times R_Z}{2 \times \pi \times L \times C_{OUT,min} \times k_{COUT}} \quad (18)$$

blocks.html: BW = \frac{12.5 \times 10^{-6} \times 1.5 \times 10^{-3} \times 2.1 \times 10^3}{2 \times \pi \times 105 \times 10^{-9} \times 195 \times 10^{-6} \times 2} = 153.1 kHz \quad (19)
blocks.markdown: $$BW = \frac{12.5 \times 10^{-6} \times 1.5 \times 10^{-3} \times 2.1 \times 10^3}{2 \times \pi \times 105 \times 10^{-9} \times 195 \times 10^{-6} \times 2} = 153.1 kHz \quad (19)$$

blocks.html: Use Equation 20 to calculate the recommended value of C_C.
blocks.markdown: Use [Equation 20](#) to calculate the recommended value of  $C_C$ .

blocks.html: C_C = \frac{k_{BW}}{2 \times \pi \times BW \times R_Z} \quad (20)
blocks.markdown: $$C_C = \frac{k_{BW}}{2 \times \pi \times BW \times R_Z} \quad (20)$$

blocks.html: C_C = \frac{4}{2 \times \pi \times 153 \times 10^3 \times 2.1 \times 10^3} = 1.981 nF \quad (21)
blocks.markdown: $$C_C = \frac{4}{2 \times \pi \times 153 \times 10^3 \times 2.1 \times 10^3} = 1.981 nF \quad (21)$$

blocks.html: The closest standard value from the E12 series is 1.8 nF.
blocks.markdown: The closest standard value from the E12 series is  $1.8 nF$ .

The diagram illustrates a stacked configuration of two TPS6287Bx devices, labeled as the Primary Device (top) and the Secondary Device (bottom). The Primary Device's VIN is connected to a 2.7 V to 6 V source. Its EN pin is driven by a voltage divider (REN) from VIO. Its SDA and SCL pins interface with an I2C bus. The VSET1 and VSET2 pins are connected to a resistive divider (RVSET1, RVSET2) to set the output voltage. The Primary Device's SW pin is connected to the load via a 100 nH inductor and a COUT capacitor. Its VOSNS and GOSNS pins are connected to the load voltage sense point. The Primary Device's COMP pin is connected to the Secondary Device's COMP pin. The Primary Device's PG pin is connected to the Secondary Device's PG pin and a power good sense resistor (RPG) to VIO. Its COMP pin is connected to the Primary Device's COMP pin. Its PG pin is connected to the Primary Device's PG pin. Its SYNC_OUT pin is connected to ground through a 47 kΩ resistor. Both devices have their AGND, GND, and GND pins connected to a common ground rail. The load is connected to the Primary Device's SW pin through a 100 nH inductor and a CLOAD capacitor. The load voltage is sensed by the Primary Device's VOSNS and GOSNS pins. The Primary Device's SW pin is also connected to the Secondary Device's SW pin through a 100 nH inductor and a COUT capacitor. The Primary Device's SW pin is also connected to the load through a 100 nH inductor and a CLOAD capacitor. The load is connected to the Primary Device's SW pin through a 100 nH inductor and a CLOAD capacitor.

blocks.html: \Delta V_{OUT} = \pm V_{OUT} \times (TOL_{VOUT} - TOL_{DC}) \quad (22)
blocks.markdown: $$\Delta V_{OUT} = \pm V_{OUT} \times (TOL_{VOUT} - TOL_{DC}) \quad (22)$$

blocks.html: \Delta V_{OUT} = \pm 0.75 \times (0.04 - 0.008) = \pm 24 \text{ mV} \quad (23)
blocks.markdown: $$\Delta V_{OUT} = \pm 0.75 \times (0.04 - 0.008) = \pm 24 \text{ mV} \quad (23)$$

blocks.html: 10.4.2 Detailed Design Procedure
blocks.markdown: #### 10.4.2 Detailed Design Procedure

blocks.html: 10.4.2.1 Selecting the Compensation Resistor
blocks.markdown: ##### 10.4.2.1 Selecting the Compensation Resistor

blocks.html: The calculation for a stack of two converters is similar to the single device expect that the parameter "number of phases" NΦ is added to the equations. Use Equation 24 to calculate the recommended value of compensation resistor RZ:
blocks.markdown: The calculation for a stack of two converters is similar to the single device expect that the parameter "number of phases" N<sub>Φ</sub> is added to the equations. Use Equation 24 to calculate the recommended value of compensation resistor R<sub>Z</sub>:

blocks.html: R_Z = \frac{1}{g_m} \left( \frac{\pi \times \Delta I_{OUT} \times L}{4 \times \tau \times N_{\Phi} \times \Delta V_{OUT}} \right) (1 + TOL_{IND}) \quad (24)
blocks.markdown: $$R_Z = \frac{1}{g_m} \left( \frac{\pi \times \Delta I_{OUT} \times L}{4 \times \tau \times N_{\Phi} \times \Delta V_{OUT}} \right) (1 + TOL_{IND}) \quad (24)$$

blocks.html: R_Z = \frac{1}{1.5 \times 10^{-3}} \left( \frac{\pi \times 24 \times 105 \times 10^{-9}}{4 \times 12.5 \times 10^{-6} \times 2 \times 24 \times 10^{-3}} \right) (1 + 0.2) \Omega = 3.382 \text{ k}\Omega \quad (25)
blocks.markdown: $$R_Z = \frac{1}{1.5 \times 10^{-3}} \left( \frac{\pi \times 24 \times 105 \times 10^{-9}}{4 \times 12.5 \times 10^{-6} \times 2 \times 24 \times 10^{-3}} \right) (1 + 0.2) \Omega = 3.382 \text{ k}\Omega \quad (25)$$

blocks.html: Rounding up, the closest standard value from the E24 series is 3.3kΩ.
blocks.markdown: Rounding up, the closest standard value from the E24 series is 3.3kΩ.

blocks.html: 10.4.2.2 Selecting the Output Capacitors
blocks.markdown: ##### 10.4.2.2 Selecting the Output Capacitors

blocks.html: If the converter remains in regulation, the minimum output capacitance required is given by:
blocks.markdown: If the converter remains in regulation, the minimum output capacitance required is given by:

blocks.html: C_{OUT(min)(reg)} = \left( \frac{\tau \times g_m \times R_Z}{2 \times \pi \times \frac{L}{N_\phi} \times \frac{f_{SW}}{4}} \right) \left( 1 + \sqrt{TOL_{IND}^2 + TOL_{fSW}^2} \right) \quad (26)
blocks.markdown: $$C_{OUT(min)(reg)} = \left( \frac{\tau \times g_m \times R_Z}{2 \times \pi \times \frac{L}{N_\phi} \times \frac{f_{SW}}{4}} \right) \left( 1 + \sqrt{TOL_{IND}^2 + TOL_{fSW}^2} \right) \quad (26)$$

blocks.html: C_{OUT(min)(reg)} = \left( \frac{12.5 \times 10^{-6} \times 1.5 \times 10^{-3} \times 3.3 \times 10^3}{2 \times \pi \times \frac{105 \times 10^{-9}}{2} \times \frac{1.5 \times 10^6}{4}} \right) \left( 1 + \sqrt{20\%^2 + 10\%^2} \right) F = 612.7 \mu F \quad (27)
blocks.markdown: $$C_{OUT(min)(reg)} = \left( \frac{12.5 \times 10^{-6} \times 1.5 \times 10^{-3} \times 3.3 \times 10^3}{2 \times \pi \times \frac{105 \times 10^{-9}}{2} \times \frac{1.5 \times 10^6}{4}} \right) \left( 1 + \sqrt{20\%^2 + 10\%^2} \right) F = 612.7 \mu F \quad (27)$$

blocks.html: If the converter loop saturates, the minimum output capacitance is given by:
blocks.markdown: If the converter loop saturates, the minimum output capacitance is given by:

blocks.html: C_{OUT(min)(sat)} = \frac{1}{\Delta V_{OUT}} \left( \frac{\frac{L}{N_\phi} \times \left( \Delta I_{OUT} + \frac{I_{L(PP)}}{2} \right)^2}{2 \times V_{OUT}} - \frac{\Delta I_{OUT} \times t_t}{2} \right) (1 + TOL_{IND}) \quad (28)
blocks.markdown: $$C_{OUT(min)(sat)} = \frac{1}{\Delta V_{OUT}} \left( \frac{\frac{L}{N_\phi} \times \left( \Delta I_{OUT} + \frac{I_{L(PP)}}{2} \right)^2}{2 \times V_{OUT}} - \frac{\Delta I_{OUT} \times t_t}{2} \right) (1 + TOL_{IND}) \quad (28)$$

blocks.html: C_{OUT(min)(sat)} = \frac{1}{24 \times 10^{-3}} \left( \frac{105 \times 10^{-9} \times \left( 24 + \frac{1.84}{2} \right)^2}{2 \times 0.75} - \frac{24 \times 1 \times 10^{-6}}{2} \right) (1 + 20\%) F = 623 \mu F \quad (29)
blocks.markdown: $$C_{OUT(min)(sat)} = \frac{1}{24 \times 10^{-3}} \left( \frac{105 \times 10^{-9} \times \left( 24 + \frac{1.84}{2} \right)^2}{2 \times 0.75} - \frac{24 \times 1 \times 10^{-6}}{2} \right) (1 + 20\%) F = 623 \mu F \quad (29)$$

blocks.html: In this case, choose C_{OUT(min)} = 623 \mu F, as the larger of the two values, for the output capacitance.
blocks.markdown: In this case, choose  $C_{OUT(min)} = 623 \mu F$ , as the larger of the two values, for the output capacitance.

blocks.html: When calculating worst-case component values, use the value calculated above as the minimum output capacitance required. For ceramic capacitors, the nominal capacitance when considering tolerance, DC bias, temperature, and aging effects is typically two times the minimum capacitance. In this case the nominal capacitance is thus 1246 \mu F.
blocks.markdown: When calculating worst-case component values, use the value calculated above as the *minimum* output capacitance required. For ceramic capacitors, the *nominal* capacitance when considering tolerance, DC bias, temperature, and aging effects is typically two times the minimum capacitance. In this case the nominal capacitance is thus  $1246 \mu F$ .

blocks.html: 10.4.2.3 Selecting the Compensation Capacitor C_C
blocks.markdown: ##### 10.4.2.3 Selecting the Compensation Capacitor $C_C$

blocks.html: BW = \frac{\tau \times g_m \times R_Z}{2 \times \pi \times \frac{L}{N_\phi} \times C_{OUT,min} \times k_{COUT}} \quad (30)
blocks.markdown: $$BW = \frac{\tau \times g_m \times R_Z}{2 \times \pi \times \frac{L}{N_\phi} \times C_{OUT,min} \times k_{COUT}} \quad (30)$$

blocks.html: BW = \frac{12.5 \times 10^{-6} \times 1.5 \times 10^{-3} \times 3.3 \times 10^3}{2 \times \pi \times \frac{105 \times 10^{-9}}{2} \times 623 \times 10^{-6} \times 2} = 150.5 \text{ kHz} \quad (31)
blocks.markdown: $$BW = \frac{12.5 \times 10^{-6} \times 1.5 \times 10^{-3} \times 3.3 \times 10^3}{2 \times \pi \times \frac{105 \times 10^{-9}}{2} \times 623 \times 10^{-6} \times 2} = 150.5 \text{ kHz} \quad (31)$$

blocks.html: Next, calculate C_C:
blocks.markdown: Next, calculate  $C_C$ :

blocks.html: C_C = \frac{k_{BW}}{2 \times \pi \times BW \times R_Z} \quad (32)
blocks.markdown: $$C_C = \frac{k_{BW}}{2 \times \pi \times BW \times R_Z} \quad (32)$$

blocks.html: C_C = \frac{4}{2 \times \pi \times 150.5 \times 10^3 \times 3.3 \times 10^3} = 1.282 \text{ nF} \quad (33)
blocks.markdown: $$C_C = \frac{4}{2 \times \pi \times 150.5 \times 10^3 \times 3.3 \times 10^3} = 1.282 \text{ nF} \quad (33)$$

blocks.html: The closest standard value from the E12 series is 1.5 \text{ nF}.
blocks.markdown: The closest standard value from the E12 series is  $1.5 \text{ nF}$ .

blocks.html: The TPS6287Bxx device family has no special requirements for input power supply. The input power supply output current must be rated according to the supply voltage, output voltage, and output current of the TPS6287Bxx.
blocks.markdown: The TPS6287Bxx device family has no special requirements for input power supply. The input power supply output current must be rated according to the supply voltage, output voltage, and output current of the TPS6287Bxx.

blocks.html: 10.7 Layout
blocks.markdown: ### 10.7 Layout

blocks.html: Achieving the performance the TPS6287Bxx devices are capable of requires proper PDN and PCB design. TI therefore recommends the user perform a power integrity analysis on the design. There are a number of commercially available power integrity software tools, and the user can use these tools to model the effects on performance of the PCB layout and passive components.
blocks.markdown: Achieving the performance the TPS6287Bxx devices are capable of requires proper PDN and PCB design. TI therefore recommends the user perform a power integrity analysis on the design. There are a number of commercially available power integrity software tools, and the user can use these tools to model the effects on performance of the PCB layout and passive components.

blocks.html: In addition to the use of power integrity tools, TI recommends the following basic principles:
blocks.markdown: In addition to the use of power integrity tools, TI recommends the following basic principles:

blocks.html:
• • Place the input capacitors close to the VIN and GND pins. Position the input capacitors in order of increasing size, starting with the smallest capacitors closest to the VIN and GND pins. Use an identical layout for both VIN-GND pin pairs of the package, to gain maximum benefit from the butterfly configuration.
  • • Place the inductor close to the device and keep the SW node small.
blocks.markdown:
- Place the input capacitors close to the VIN and GND pins. Position the input capacitors in order of increasing size, starting with the smallest capacitors closest to the VIN and GND pins. Use an identical layout for both VIN-GND pin pairs of the package, to gain maximum benefit from the butterfly configuration.
- Place the inductor close to the device and keep the SW node small.

blocks.html:
• • Connect the exposed thermal pad and the GND pins of the device together. Use multiple thermal vias to connect the exposed thermal pad of the device to one or more ground planes (TI's EVM uses nine 150µm thermal vias).
  • • Use multiple power and ground planes.
  • • Route the VOSNS and GOSNS remote sense lines on the primary device as a differential pair and connect them to the lowest-impedance point of the PDN. If the desired connection point is not the lowest impedance point of the PDN, optimize the PDN until the desired connection point is the lowest impedance point of the PDN. Do not route the VOSNS and GOSNS close to any of the switch nodes.
  • • Connect the compensation components between COMP and AGND. Do not connect the compensation components directly to power ground.
  • • If possible, distribute the output capacitors evenly between the TPS6287Bxx device and the point-of-load, rather than placing them altogether in one place.
  • • Use multiple vias to connect each capacitor pad to the power and ground planes (TI's EVM typically uses four vias per pad).
  • • Use plenty of stitching vias to make sure of a low impedance connection between different power and ground planes.
blocks.markdown:
- Connect the exposed thermal pad and the GND pins of the device together. Use multiple thermal vias to connect the exposed thermal pad of the device to one or more ground planes (TI's EVM uses nine 150µm thermal vias).
- Use multiple power and ground planes.
- Route the VOSNS and GOSNS remote sense lines on the primary device as a differential pair and connect them to the lowest-impedance point of the PDN. If the desired connection point is not the lowest impedance point of the PDN, optimize the PDN until the desired connection point is the lowest impedance point of the PDN. Do not route the VOSNS and GOSNS close to any of the switch nodes.
- Connect the compensation components between COMP and AGND. Do not connect the compensation components directly to power ground.
- If possible, distribute the output capacitors evenly between the TPS6287Bxx device and the point-of-load, rather than placing them altogether in one place.
- Use multiple vias to connect each capacitor pad to the power and ground planes (TI's EVM typically uses four vias per pad).
- Use plenty of stitching vias to make sure of a low impedance connection between different power and ground planes.
